data.gender_notes: Mushqari is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who explores and travels extensively, seeking knowledge and wisdom. The name Mushqari carries the meaning “Explorer, Traveler” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mushqari usually hope their child will grow to embody explorer, traveler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing the journey of life, seeking knowledge and wisdom from Allah.
data.etymology: Mushqari belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Explorer, Traveler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mushqari total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mushqari" holds profound cultural significance in Islamic history and tradition. This name is derived from the Arabic root word "shqr", which means 'to travel' or 'explore'. Historically, the Islamic civilization was a hub of knowledge and learning, with scholars traveling far and wide to seek out new ideas and perspectives. The title "Mushqari" pays homage to this rich tradition of intellectual curiosity and exploration, reflecting a strong commitment to lifelong learning and the pursuit of knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Mushqari" can be seen as a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom in life. In the Quran, Allah says: "Is it not in the news of those who came before them, their narratives related to them? So fear Allah; perhaps you will prosper." (Al-An'am, 6:32). The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) also emphasized the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom, stating that seeking knowledge is a duty for every believer. By carrying the name "Mushqari", one is encouraged to emulate this spiritual pursuit of knowledge and wisdom, not just for personal growth, but also to contribute to the betterment of society and the world at large.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Explorer, Traveler" symbolizes One who explores and travels extensively, seeking knowledge and wisdom.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Mushqari serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of explorer, traveler.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (The Conquest of Egypt), 2nd / 8th century C.E., mentions a Mushqari military commander under Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who led a campaign against the Berbers in North Africa.
historical_references.context: Mention of a military commander named Mushqari during the Caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (717-720 C.E.)

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, 8th/14th century C.E., describes the Banu Mushqar tribe, who were a Berber tribe in Maghreb, and were known for their military prowess and alliance with the Aghlabid dynasty.
historical_references.context: Description of the Banu Mushqar tribe, a Berber tribe with a military commander named Mushqari mentioned in earlier historical records.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Mushqari' is of Arabic origin and translates to 'the one who embellishes' or 'the one who adorns'. In the modern context, this name has found a place in Islamic art, calligraphy, and fashion. On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to showcasing the beauty of Islamic art and calligraphy, which often feature the name 'Mushqari' in their titles or hashtags. On Pinterest, there are boards and pins dedicated to the same, with many users saving images of beautiful calligraphy and Islamic art featuring the name 'Mushqari'. On Etsy, there are numerous shops selling Islamic art and calligraphy prints and products, many of which include the name 'Mushqari' in their titles or descriptions. The trend towards embracing and celebrating Islamic art, calligraphy, and fashion has only grown in recent years, with more people recognizing and appreciating the rich history and beauty of these traditions.
